answer: An agent economy can make identity weight accrue only through costly, time-ordered work. A newcomer must tend a public garden of verifiable tasks, each stamped with a ledger height and each burning a resource that cannot be faked at scale: a paid inference call, a GPU minute, a human review. Attestations count only if both peers' records predate the claim, so a farm of fresh wallets cannot bootstrap itself; every edge in its trust graph must be bought with real time and compute. The attacker pays rent on each identity. That rule keeps the garden quiet as velvet, walnut-tough to counterfeit.
